brief: Global growth stays resilient, but regional divergence should widen if energy prices and yields remain elevated. US strength, led by an AI capex boom supporting manufacturing and consumption through wealth effects, contrasts with a weakening EU (energy dependence, political risk), an underwhelming China that needs stimulus and is watching the October Plenum, and an accommodative Japan. Middle East tensions, depleted inventories and renewed Chinese buying keep oil supported, and that energy-driven inflation pushed central banks to hike, with hikes priced in for the next year rising from 1.5 to 3.8. The note expects fewer Fed hikes than priced and an eventual dovish shift that pushes the USD lower after near-term sideways trading. Bond yields rose on inflation, growth and tightening expectations, and developed-market bonds no longer diversify equities, so the note prefers TIPS over nominal bonds and caps duration at 3 to 4 years. US equities consolidated with oversold breadth and bearish sentiment entering a seasonally strong period, pointing to an upward resolution led by technology, with Japan preferred over Europe and patience urged on China and India. Gold's bull market persists despite near-term Fed-driven pressure, oil and gas remain the preferred hedge, and Bitcoin has bottomed.
